haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent: no row and no email.
haiku-low.q2: Nothing is sent and no row is created; the user sees the same generic message, and the existing live link is kept.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = issued_at + 30m). It ends sooner if the link is used, or replaced by a newer link, which sets dead_at.
haiku-low.q4: Still live. The password is validated before the burn, so the form is re-shown with the reason and the link stays usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted on every device, including this one. The user is redirected to /login and logs in by hand.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times, then logs and drops the job. Nobody is told, and the user gets no signal and must request again.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is put in the emailed link and briefly in the queued mail job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and looks for a live row (dead_at NULL, expires_at later than now). Found shows the form; not found shows the expired page.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table: the count of the user's rows with issued_at in the last hour. Old rows fall out of the window by time; a daily delete removes rows older than 1 day.
haiku-low.q10: At request step 5, inside the same transaction and before the new row is inserted, earlier unused links get dead_at set, so they are killed. The rows are kept.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: the password hash is updated, the token is burned, and all the user's sessions are deleted. The confirmation email is enqueued only after the commit.
haiku-low.q12: The burn is one conditional UPDATE (dead_at IS NULL and expires_at > now()). Only one submit matches the row; the other updates zero rows and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200 message ("If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link."). Nothing is sent: no row, no email.
sonnet.q2: Nothing is sent: no row, no job, existing link untouched. The user still gets the same generic 200 message. The limit is 3 per rolling hour, and the request is rolled back.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = issued_at + 30m). It ends sooner when it is used, or when a newer link replaces it (dead_at is set).
sonnet.q4: Still live and usable until it expires. The form is re-shown with the reason, and nothing is written.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including the current device. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in by hand with the new password. No session is created.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told: no signal, no alert. The old link was already killed, so they must re-request, and that counts toward 3/hour.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated in the API server at request time (32 random bytes). The link containing it goes into the enqueued mail job ({to, link with raw}), and the worker sends that email. Only sha256(raw) is stored in the DB.
sonnet.q8: The server computes h = sha256(RAW) from the token query parameter and looks for a live link with token_hash = h (dead_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()). If found it shows the new-password form. If not found it shows the "expired" page. Unknown, expired, used and replaced links all look the same.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept in a separate counter. It is the count of rows in password_reset_tokens for that user with issued_at > now() - 1h, including used and replaced rows. Old requests drop out of the count when their issued_at is more than an hour old. A periodic delete (e.g. daily) removes rows older than 1 day.
sonnet.q10: All the user's earlier live links are marked dead (dead_at = now()) in the same transaction as the new insert. This happens in step 5, after the rate-limit check passes and before the new row is inserted (step 6) and the COMMIT (step 7). It is done while holding the user row lock.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is burned (dead_at set), users.password_hash is updated, and all of the user's sessions rows are deleted. Then COMMIT. The "password was changed" email is enqueued after the COMMIT (step 4), outside the transaction.
sonnet.q12: The burn is a single conditional UPDATE (WHERE token_hash=... AND dead_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id). One submit wins and gets 1 row. The other gets 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the "expired" page.
